The panties were cut high on the thigh, designed to display rather than cover, and he stood before them with his exposure complete, his shame total.

"Lovely," Claire breathed. "Elise, where did you find that piece?"

"Specialty shop online," Elise replied. "They cater to... specific arrangements. The plug is silicone, weighted, designed for extended wear. He'll have it in until I decide to remove it. Which will likely be after you both leave."

"You're cruel," Diana said, but her voice held admiration.

"I'm thorough," Elise corrected. "Melody needs to understand that his body is not his own. That every part of him belongs to me until his debt is paid. And even then, we may need to discuss... alternative arrangements."

Melody let the dress fall back into place, his hands shaking so badly he could barely control them. The conversation continued around him, Elise and her friends discussing him as if he were not present, or as if his presence were irrelevant to the discussion of his own fate. They spoke of training techniques, of psychological conditioning, of the pleasure of watching a man learn to accept his submission. They spoke of other men Elise had known, other debts that had been paid in service, other transformations that had been wrought in this very apartment.

Through it all, Melody stood. The plug shifted with every breath, every subtle movement, a constant reminder of his position. His cheeks burned with the blush that Claire had found so amusing, and he could hear the quiet laughter behind him whenever one of them made a particularly pointed observation about his situation, his training, his future.

"Spin for us again, Melody," Claire said eventually, her voice warm with wine and amusement. "I want to see how you move in those heels."

Melody looked to Elise, who nodded permission, her eyes cold and bright with satisfaction. He turned slowly, carefully, the plug shifting inside him with every degree of rotation, his cheeks burning as he heard the quiet laughter behind him, the appreciative murmurs, the clink of wine glasses being raised in toast to his humiliation. He completed the turn and stood before them, exposed in every possible way, and waited for whatever would come next.

The evening had only begun.

lib.title: The Shoe Ritual
lib.md:
The clock on the mantelpiece had struck eleven before Claire and Diana finally rose to leave, their departure delayed by endless glasses of wine and conversation that seemed to circle ever closer to Melody, to his situation, to the entertainment his humiliation provided. They had made him serve them throughout the evening—refilling glasses, arranging cheese plates, standing at attention while they discussed his training, his debt, his increasingly ambiguous future. Each command had been delivered with the casualness of royalty addressing a servant, and Melody had obeyed each with the desperate precision of a man who knows that disobedience is not an option.

Now the apartment was silent again, save for the ticking of that same mantel clock and the distant sound of traffic from the street below. The living room smelled of wine and perfume and the ghost of women's laughter, a scent that seemed to cling to the velvet furniture and the heavy curtains. Melody stood where Elise had instructed him to remain, near the door where he had seen her guests out, his legs aching from hours of standing, his cheeks still warm with the accumulated humiliation of the evening.

Elise had not moved from the emerald sofa. She sat with her legs crossed, one arm draped along the back of the cushions, her wine glass empty now, her eyes fixed on Melody with an expression he had learned to recognize—a look of assessment, of consideration, of a collector examining a piece that had just been displayed for visitors and must now be returned to its proper storage.

"Close the door," she said. "Lock it."

Melody turned, his movements careful and deliberate, the plug still seated firmly inside him, a presence that had become almost familiar over the course of the evening, though no less intrusive. He turned the deadbolt, the sound loud in the quiet apartment, and when he turned back, Elise had shifted her position. She had uncrossed her legs and extended them slightly, her feet in those black heels—Louboutins, he knew, though he had not been permitted to handle them until now—resting on the Persian rug that covered the center of the floor.

"Come here," she said.

Melody walked toward her, each step sending new sensations through him, the plug shifting with his movement, the heels clicking against the hardwood and then muffled by the rug's thick pile. He stopped before her, standing at a respectful distance, his hands clasped behind his back in the position she preferred when he was awaiting instruction.

"Kneel," Elise said.

The command was simple, direct, and Melody obeyed without hesitation, lowering himself to the rug, feeling the rough wool against his knees, the shift in position sending a fresh wave of sensation from the plug that made him gasp involuntarily. He kept his eyes lowered, trained on the floor, though he could see her feet in his peripheral vision, the sharp lines of the heels, the gleaming black leather, the red soles that were the signature of their maker.

Elise leaned forward, her elbows resting on her knees, and when she spoke, her voice was lower than before, intimate in a way that was somehow worse than the public humiliation of her friends' presence. "You did well tonight," she said. "You didn't stumble. You didn't spill anything. You didn't make a sound when Claire touched your face, when Diana commented on your... preparation."

"Thank you, ma'am," Melody whispered.

"Don't thank me yet," Elise replied. "The evening isn't over. My feet hurt. These shoes were not designed for six hours of entertaining. They were designed to be admired, to elevate, to transform. But they are not comfortable. Do you understand what I'm telling you, Melody?"

He understood. He had understood from the moment she had extended her legs, from the tone in her voice when she spoke of her feet. He understood that this was part of his service, part of his debt, part of the endless series of tasks and trials that Elise devised to remind him of his place.

"I understand, ma'am," he said.

"Remove them," Elise instructed. "With your teeth. Carefully. These cost more than you earned in a month at your old job. I don't want them scratched. I don't want them damaged. I want you to grip the back of the heel between your lips and slide them off with the same care you might use if you were undressing a lover. Do you understand?"

Melody's hands trembled where they were clasped behind his back. He looked up at her, seeking confirmation, and she nodded, her expression cold and amused, her dark eyes glittering in the lamplight. He shifted forward on his knees, moving closer to her feet, close enough to smell the leather, close enough to see the way the material had molded to her feet over the evening, the slight impression of her toes visible through the glossy surface.

He leaned forward, his balance precarious on his knees, his body forced to adjust around the plug with every movement. The first shoe—the right one—was angled slightly toward him, the heel pointing outward, and he positioned himself carefully, his heart hammering in his chest, his face burning with the knowledge of what he was about to do, of how far he had fallen, of how completely Elise had transformed him from the man he had been into this creature that knelt before her, preparing to remove her shoes with his mouth.

He parted his lips and took the back of the heel between them.

The leather was smooth against his lips, cool and slightly yielding, smelling of polish and Elise's skin and something else—the faint scent of the street, of the walk from the car to the apartment door, of the places she had been while he waited for her return. He gripped it carefully, his teeth not quite touching the surface, his lips forming a seal around the curved shape, and he began to pull.

It required more force than he had expected. The shoe was fitted snugly to her foot, molded by hours of wear to the shape of her heel, and Melody had to rock backward slightly, using his own weight to create the necessary leverage. The plug shifted inside him with the movement, sending a jolt of sensation through his body that made him gasp around the leather, his breath hot against the material. He pulled steadily, trembling with the effort of maintaining his grip, trembling with humiliation, trembling with the knowledge that Elise was watching every moment of this, cataloging every indignity, storing away every detail for future reference.

The shoe began to slide. He felt the resistance give way, felt the leather slide against her stockinged heel, felt the way her foot lifted slightly to assist him, not out of kindness but out of impatience, out of the desire to see him complete this task, to witness his submission in yet another form. The heel emerged from the shoe, and Melody followed it with his mouth, maintaining his grip until the shoe was completely free of her foot, until he was holding it dangling from his lips like a dog retrieving a toy, like a servant performing a task so debasing that it stripped away the last remnants of dignity he had managed to preserve.

He lowered the shoe carefully to the rug beside him, releasing it from his mouth with a wet sound that seemed obscenely loud in the quiet room. His lips felt swollen, marked by the pressure of the leather, and he could taste the polish now, bitter and chemical on his tongue, mixed with the salt of his own sweat and the humiliation that seemed to have become a physical substance, a flavor he could not escape.

"Good," Elise said, and there was satisfaction in her voice, the satisfaction of a trainer whose animal has performed a trick correctly. "Now the other one. And Melody—don't rush. I want to feel your care. I want to know that you understand the value of what you're handling."

He shifted his position, moving to her left foot, his knees sore from the rug's rough texture, his thighs aching from the hours of standing, his entire body a catalog of discomfort that was entirely secondary to the psychological torture of his situation. He leaned forward again, positioning himself carefully, and took the back of the left heel between his lips.

This time, he tried to be more deliberate, more careful, to infuse the act with the reverence Elise seemed to demand. He gripped the leather firmly but gently, his lips soft around the hard shape, and he pulled with a steady, trembling pressure that required him to rock back on his heels, to arch his back, to present himself in a posture of complete submission. The plug pressed against him with the movement, a constant reminder of his place, of his debt, of the fact that his body was not his own and had not been his own for six months.

The shoe slid free more easily this time, or perhaps he had simply learned the angle, the necessary force, the way to move his body to accomplish this task without damaging the leather, without disappointing her. He lowered it to the rug beside its mate, releasing it from his mouth, and sat back on his heels, his breath coming in shallow gasps, his face burning, his eyes fixed on the floor between her feet.

Elise flexed her toes, now freed from the constriction of the heels, and Melody could see the marks the shoes had left on her skin—faint red lines across her instep, a slight indentation where the strap had buckled, the evidence of the evening's discomfort that he was expected to address. She leaned back against the sofa cushions, her legs still extended, her feet now bare except for the sheer stockings she wore.

"Look at me, Melody," she said.

He raised his eyes, meeting her gaze, and what he saw there made his stomach clench. She was smiling, but it was not a warm smile, not a kind smile. It was the smile of someone who has complete power over another, who recognizes no equality, who sees in his humiliation not tragedy but entertainment, not cruelty but necessity.

"You performed adequately tonight," she said. "My friends were impressed. Claire commented, after you stepped out to refill the ice bucket, on how well-trained you are. She asked if I would consider loaning you out for a weekend, so that she might experience your service for herself. I told her I would consider it. Do you understand what that means, Melody?"

He understood. The thought of serving Claire, of being transferred to another woman's home, of performing these same rituals for a stranger while Elise was not present to moderate, to control, to protect him from consequences she had not yet chosen to impose—it filled him with a terror that was only slightly less powerful than the humiliation of his current position.

"I understand, ma'am," he managed, his voice barely above a whisper.

"Good," Elise said. "But that is a concern for another time. Tonight, you have a task to complete. My feet are tired. My shoes have been worn for hours. They need cleaning. And you, Melody, are going to clean them."

She gestured toward the shoes where they sat on the rug, and Melody felt his stomach drop, felt the blood drain from his face only to rush back in a fresh wave of heat. He had hoped—foolishly, he realized now—that removing the shoes would be the end of it, that he would be permitted to massage her feet, perhaps, or to prepare her bath, or to retire to his room to wait for whatever morning would bring. But Elise was not finished with him. Elise was never finished with him until she had extracted every possible measure of submission, until she had pushed him to the edge of what he could endure and then slightly beyond.

"With your tongue," Elise clarified, her voice conversational, as if she were discussing the weather or the stock market. "I want you to lick the soles clean. The leather has touched the ground. It has touched the floor of my car. It has accumulated dust and dirt and the residue of the evening. You are going to remove that residue with your mouth. You are going to clean my shoes as thoroughly as any shoeshine boy on any street corner, with the added benefit that you will be using your tongue instead of a brush. Do you understand?"

Melody's hands clenched behind his back, his fingers digging into his own wrists, the only outlet for the rebellion that screamed inside him, the voice that said this was too much, that this crossed some line from service into degradation so profound that he would never recover from it, that he would be marked by this moment for the rest of his life, whatever that life might look like when his debt was finally paid.

But he was already marked. He had been marked from the moment he signed the contract, from the moment he accepted her terms, from the moment he first knelt before her and understood that his dignity was a currency he had already spent.

"I understand, ma'am," he said.

"Begin with the right shoe," Elise instructed. "The sole, Melody. I want to see your tongue on the leather. I want to see you press your face to the bottom of my shoe and clean it as if your life depended on it. Because in a very real way, Melody, your life does depend on it. Your life here. Your position. Your eventual freedom. All of it depends on your willingness to serve, to submit, to accept your place."

Melody reached for the shoe with trembling hands, lifting it from the rug, feeling the weight of it, the warmth that still lingered from her foot. He turned it over, exposing the red sole, the signature color that seemed to glow in the lamplight, the leather slightly scuffed from an evening of wear, marked with faint traces of dust and dirt that he could see even in the dim light. The sole was not filthy—Elise did not walk through mud or grime, did not subject her possessions to unnecessary roughness—but it was worn, used, marked by the evening's activities, and he was expected to remove those marks with his tongue.

He lowered his head, positioning the shoe before his face, and extended his tongue.

The leather was dry against his tongue, slightly rough, textured in a way that the polished upper was not. He pressed his tongue flat against the surface and dragged it upward, from the toe toward the heel, and tasted immediately the bitterness of the street, the chemical residue of polish, the faint salt of his own sweat where his hands had touched the shoe earlier in the evening. The flavor was complex and unpleasant, a physical manifestation of his degradation that he could not escape by closing his eyes, by looking away, by pretending this was not happening.

He licked again, following the curve of the sole, his tongue moving in broad strokes that covered the red leather with saliva, that began to dissolve the accumulated dust, that left wet trails across the surface in patterns that seemed almost obscene in their irregularity. The shoe smelled strongly now, the scent of leather mixed with the scent of his own mouth, his own submission, the pheromones of humiliation that seemed to fill the air between them.

"Press harder," Elise instructed, her voice coming from above him, from somewhere distant though she had not moved. "I want to feel the pressure through the shoe. I want to know that you're not holding back, that you're not trying to preserve some last shred of dignity by being delicate. Clean it, Melody. Clean it properly."

Melody pressed harder, his tongue flattening against the leather, the texture rough against the sensitive surface, the taste growing stronger with each pass. He worked systematically, starting at the toe and moving toward the heel, covering the entire surface of the sole with his saliva, with his attention, with the complete focus that Elise demanded of him. He could feel the shape of the shoe, the way it curved to match the arch of her foot, the slight wear pattern where her weight had settled over the evening.

The plug shifted inside him as he moved, a constant reminder of his position, of his preparation, of the fact that he had been ready for this evening before he even knew what it would entail. He was dizzy with humiliation, with the physical reality of what he was doing, with the knowledge that Elise was watching every moment, cataloging every lick, storing away every detail of his submission for future use, for future entertainment, for the stories she would tell her friends about the man who had licked her shoes clean after an evening of wine and conversation.

"Good," Elise said, after what felt like hours but was probably only minutes. "Now the heel. The sides. Don't miss anything, Melody. I expect thoroughness. I expect dedication. I expect you to treat this task as if it were the most important thing you have ever done, because in this moment, it is. In this moment, nothing else exists but you and my shoe and your tongue."

Melody moved to the heel, turning the shoe in his hands, exposing the narrow strip of leather that had supported Elise's weight all evening, that had elevated her above the ground, above the street, above the level of ordinary existence. He pressed his tongue to the heel and dragged it upward, feeling the change in texture, the way the leather was smoother here, worn by contact with the ground, marked by the places it had touched.

He worked his way around the heel, his tongue moving in circles, covering every inch of the surface, tasting the residue of the evening, the faint metallic tang of the street, the chemical bitterness of the polish that had been applied to keep the leather supple and dark. His jaw ached from the effort, from the unfamiliar motion, from the necessity of keeping his mouth open, of extending his tongue, of pressing it against the unyielding surface again and again.

When he had finished with the heel, he moved to the sides of the sole, the narrow edges where the red leather met the black, where the craftsmanship of the shoe was most evident, where the cost of the item was most clearly displayed. He licked these areas carefully, his tongue tracing the seam between colors, his saliva darkening the leather in streaks that would dry eventually, that would leave no trace of his service except in his memory, in his knowledge of what he had done.

"The other shoe," Elise said, when he had finished with the first. "And Melody—look at me while you work. I want to see your eyes. I want to see the humiliation in them. I want to know that you understand exactly what you are and exactly what you are doing."

Melody lifted his head, meeting her gaze as he reached for the second shoe, his hands shaking so badly he could barely grip the leather. He turned it over, exposing the red sole, and lowered his head again, but this time he kept his eyes raised, looking up at her from his position on the floor, his tongue extended, his face burning with the blush that she found so entertaining.

He pressed his tongue to the second shoe and began to clean.

The taste was the same—bitter, chemical, leather and street and submission—but the experience was worse because he could see her watching him, could see the cold amusement in her eyes, the satisfaction that came from witnessing his complete degradation. She watched him work with the attention of a connoisseur, her head tilted slightly, her lips curved in that smile that never reached her eyes, her body relaxed against the sofa cushions as if she were watching a performance designed specifically for her entertainment.

And it was. He understood that now, if he had not understood it before. Everything he did, every task he performed, every humiliation he endured, was a performance for Elise's pleasure. She had transformed his debt into an art form, his service into a spectacle, his submission into the central entertainment of her life. She collected his humiliations the way other women collected jewelry, displaying them for her friends, cataloging them for her own satisfaction, adding to them with every passing day.

He cleaned the second shoe with the same thoroughness he had applied to the first, his tongue moving in methodical strokes, covering every inch of the red sole, working his way from toe to heel and back again, pressing hard enough that she could feel it through the leather, that she could sense his effort, his dedication, his complete surrender to her will. His jaw ached, his tongue felt raw, his knees were numb from the pressure of the floor, and still he worked, because she had not told him to stop, because the task was not complete until she declared it so.

When he had finished, when both shoes were wet with his saliva, when the dust and residue of the evening had been removed by his tongue, he sat back on his heels again, the shoes held carefully in his hands, his eyes still raised to meet hers, waiting for her judgment, her approval, her next command.

Elise looked at the shoes, examined them with the critical eye of someone who knows the value of her possessions, who expects perfection and will accept nothing less. She reached out and took them from his hands, turning them over, inspecting the soles, the heels, the sides. She nodded, once, a small gesture that sent relief flooding through Melody's body, relief that was immediately tempered by the knowledge that this was not the end, that there would always be another task, another humiliation, another demonstration of his submission required.

"You didn't complain today," Elise said, her voice soft in the quiet room, almost gentle, though he knew better than to mistake that gentleness for kindness. "When Claire asked you to refill her glass for the fourth time, you didn't hesitate. When Diana commented on your... preparation, you didn't flinch. When I instructed you to remove my shoes with your teeth, to clean them with your tongue, you obeyed without question, without argument, without that pathetic look of resentment you used to wear when I asked you to perform simple tasks."

She leaned forward, her elbows on her knees, her face close to his, close enough that he could smell her perfume, her wine, the scent of her skin that had been pressed against the leather he had just cleaned.

"That's progress," she said. "That's improvement. Six months ago, you would have argued. You would have demanded to know why, would have insisted on your dignity, would have made this more difficult than it needed to be. Now you simply obey. You accept. You understand that your dignity is not yours to claim, that it belongs to me, that I will return it to you only when I decide you have earned it, if I ever decide that at all."

Melody held her gaze, his eyes stinging with tears he refused to shed, his body aching, his mouth tasting of leather and submission, his cheeks burning with the blush that seemed permanent now, a physical mark of his status that he could not hide and she could not miss.

"Thank you, ma'am," he whispered, because it was expected, because there was nothing else to say, because in this moment, in this apartment, in this life he had chosen when he signed the contract, there was only obedience, only submission, only the endless ritual of service that defined his existence.

Elise smiled, and this time there was something almost like warmth in it, the satisfaction of a job well done, of a transformation completed, of a man fully broken and ready to be rebuilt in her image.

"You're welcome, Melody," she said. "Now take the shoes to my closet. Put them away properly. And then come back here. We still need to address that plug you've been wearing all evening. I think you've earned its removal, don't you?"

"Yes, ma'am," Melody said, rising carefully, his legs stiff, his balance uncertain, the plug shifting inside him with the movement.

He took the shoes—her shoes, the shoes he had cleaned with his tongue, the shoes that had walked through the evening while he waited and served and submitted—and walked toward her bedroom, toward the closet where her real possessions were kept, where his few items were hidden away in the mahogany wardrobe, where the division between their lives was made physically manifest in the arrangement of space and objects and value.

Behind him, he heard Elise pour herself another glass of wine, heard her settle back against the cushions, heard her sigh with the contentment of a woman who has been thoroughly entertained, who has watched her pet perform its tricks correctly, who knows that tomorrow will bring new opportunities for amusement, new chances to test the limits of his submission, new rituals to add to the endless cycle of service and humiliation that had become his life.

The evening was not over. The debt was not paid. And Melody walked carefully toward the closet, the shoes held in his trembling hands, knowing that when he returned, there would be more, there would always be more, until Elise decided there was nothing left of the man he had been and nothing remaining but the servant she had made him.

lib.title: The Interview
lib.md:
The building materialized from the afternoon haze like something summoned from a half-remembered dream, its facade constructed from smoked glass and oxidized copper that seemed to absorb the surrounding city noise rather than reflect it. Harry Lermond stood on the sidewalk for a full three minutes, clutching the printout of the email that had summoned him here, his finger tracing the embossed letterhead—*Velvet Hive Productions*—while his breath came in shallow sips that did nothing to steady the tremor in his knees. The address had led him to the warehouse district, past the abandoned textile mills and converted loft spaces, to this singular structure that rose seven stories of dark intention amid the urban decay. There were no other applicants milling about the entrance, no line of hopefuls stretching around the block as he'd imagined during the two-hour bus ride from his studio apartment on the city's fraying edge. Just a single brushed-steel door with a biometric scanner and a small brass plaque that read *Private Casting—By Appointment Only*.

He'd found the ad three days prior, wedged between postings for medical test subjects and overnight warehouse security, the kind of digital detritus one scrolls through at 3 AM when sleep refuses to come and the rent looms like a guillotine blade nine days from falling. *Content Participation Gig—Immediate Payment—No Experience Necessary—Willingness to Commit Required.* The phrase had echoed in his mind during the subsequent seventy-two hours of silence, during which he'd rehearsed his nonexistent qualifications and practiced his most agreeable smile in the cracked mirror above his bathroom sink. Now, standing before this monolith of enterprise, the smile felt like a mask he'd forgotten how to wear properly.

The interior of the Velvet Hive revealed itself in layers of deliberate obscurity. The lobby stretched wide and low, ceiling lost in shadows above, walls draped in fabric the color of dried wine that seemed to drink in the recessed lighting and redistribute it as something softer, more intimate, more insidious. Harry's cheap dress shoes—purchased two years ago for a job fair that had yielded nothing but business cards for pyramid schemes—clicked against polished concrete floors that had been treated to resemble liquid mercury. The sound died immediately, swallowed by the velvet atmosphere, as if the building itself were recording his presence and choosing to keep its own counsel.

He checked in at a desk carved from a single piece of black walnut, the receptionist's eyes never rising from her screen as she directed him to the elevator with a gesture so minimal it might have been a twitch. The lift operated without buttons, ascending smoothly to the fourth floor where the corridor narrowed and the temperature dropped five degrees. His breath began to show in faint clouds as he walked, the walls now upholstered in tufted burgundy that absorbed both sound and light, creating the sensation of moving through the throat of some great beast.

Room 407 waited at the end of the hallway, its door already ajar, spilling warm amber light into the cool corridor like an invitation or a warning.

Harry pushed through and found himself in a space that defied the industrial exterior. The studio measured perhaps twenty feet square, but the dimensions felt uncertain, elastic, as if the room breathed. The walls were draped in velvet—not the cheap synthetic of theater curtains, but something heavier, older, fabric that had weight and history and the faint scent of cedar and old perfume. The lighting came from sources he couldn't identify, warm pools of illumination that seemed to materialize from the air itself, creating zones of visibility surrounded by depths of shadow that could hide anything or nothing.

At the center stood the chair.

It was a singular piece, fixed to the floor by bolts he could see gleaming where the velveteen carpet had been cut away, the base a heavy disc of brushed steel that suggested permanence, inevitability. The upholstery matched the walls—deep plum velvet worn smooth in places, tufted with buttons that caught the light like eyes opening and closing. The armrests were wide, leather-wrapped, positioned at exact right angles to the seat. There were no wheels, no adjustment levers, no suggestion that the chair had ever been moved or would ever be moved. It faced a low table of glass and chrome, behind which sat a second chair—movable, ergonomic, professional.

Harry stood in the doorway, his hand still on the handle, suddenly aware of every inadequacy that had accumulated over twenty-eight years of living. His dress shirt, purchased from a discount chain store that specialized in last season's rejects, clung to his lower back where sweat had begun to bloom despite the room's climate-controlled coolness. The fabric was a pale blue that had faded to the color of a drowning sky after two years of wash cycles he couldn't afford to separate by color. Under his arms, damp patches spread in darkening circles, the result of the bus ride—two transfers, standing room only, the air thick with the particular bouquet of public transportation that clung to his jeans like a second skin. The denim had been dark once, now worn to the color of dirty water at the knees and thighs, carrying the olfactory signature of diesel fumes, strangers' cologne, and his own mounting anxiety.

He stepped forward because standing in the doorway felt more vulnerable than entering, and lowered himself into the fixed chair.

The velvet welcomed him with a warmth that felt almost sentient, cradling his spine in a way that should have been comforting but instead suggested capture. The seat was positioned so that his knees rose slightly higher than his hips, tilting his pelvis back, forcing his shoulders to press against the fabric. He tried to shift, to find a more assertive posture, but the chair held him in its configuration, the fixed armrests preventing him from spreading his elbows wide in the masculine pose he'd practiced. Instead, his arms fell naturally inward, hands coming to rest on his thighs where he could feel the tremor in his fingers through the thin denim.

The door clicked shut behind him, though he hadn't seen anyone enter.

Odessa Thorn sat across from him with the composure of someone who had never known the particular humiliation of unemployment, never felt the hollow in the stomach that opened when the savings account reached zero, never rehearsed lies about "between opportunities" for relatives who called less and less frequently. She was arranged in her chair with the precision of a museum display, her tailored blouse—ivory silk that caught the light like liquid bone—fitting her torso without a single wrinkle despite the hour. The pencil skirt, charcoal gray and falling exactly to the knee, maintained its creases with architectural certainty. Her heels, subtle black patent leather with a modest three-inch lift, were crossed at the ankle in a pose that suggested both accessibility and absolute control.

Her face was a study in professional neutrality—features that might have been beautiful if they ever relaxed into expression, but which remained instead in a state of pleasant potential. Her eyes were the color of faded denim, almost gray, and they regarded him with the same detachment one might extend to a spreadsheet or a weather report. Her hair, dark and pulled back into a chignon so tight it seemed to stretch her features slightly upward, caught the light in individual strands that suggested expensive maintenance. She held a tablet in one hand, the screen glowing softly, and a manila folder in the other, the kind that contained documents that changed lives.

"Mr. Lermond," she said, and her voice was the room's temperature made audible—warm on the surface with something cooler beneath. "Thank you for coming. We found you online."

The statement hung in the air between them, neither question nor accusation, simply fact delivered with the weight of inevitability. Harry's throat clicked dryly as he swallowed, his tongue feeling thick and alien in his mouth. "Found me?" he managed, the words coming out higher than he'd intended, cracking slightly on the second syllable.

"Your digital footprint," Odessa elaborated, her eyes dropping to the tablet where her finger scrolled with languid precision. "Social media profiles dormant for eight months. Employment history—retail associate, data entry clerk, food service, all positions terminated or expired within the last fourteen months. Credit score 580. Current residence—a studio apartment in the Carver District, rent due in nine days. Bank account balance: $247.33."

Each data point landed like a small stone dropped into still water, ripples of exposure spreading outward. Harry felt his face flush, the heat climbing from his collar to his cheekbones as she recited his failures with the same tone she might use for weather statistics. He wanted to protest, to explain that the retail position had been seasonal, that the data entry job had outsourced to automation, that he was looking, always looking, submitting twenty applications a day to positions he was overqualified for or underqualified for or exactly qualified for but never heard back from. The July heat settled over Jane's Victorian home like a damp wool blanket, thick and suffocating, transforming the garden into a greenhouse of humid stagnation. Stan wiped his forehead with the back of his glove, leaving a streak of dirt across his skin that mixed immediately with fresh sweat. He had been trimming the hedges for nearly two hours—an overgrown labyrinth of boxwood and privet that Jane allowed to grow wild until it threatened to consume the cobblestone paths entirely. His t-shirt, once a heather gray, had darkened to charcoal between his shoulder blades and along his spine, the cotton plastered against his skin with the kind of intimate saturation that only came from honest labor in high summer.

Three months ago, when Stan had first stepped onto Jane's property to discuss the commission—custom built-in cabinetry for her study, a reproduction oak mantelpiece, various pieces of period-appropriate furniture to fill the empty rooms of the sprawling house—he had been a different man entirely. His shoulders had filled out his work shirts with the dense muscle of a man who lifted heavy things regularly, who spent weekends at the gym maintaining the physique he'd built over years of disciplined training. His waist had been trim, his chest defined, his arms capable of hauling oak beams single-handedly without strain.

Now, as he reached upward to clip an unruly branch that arched over the garden path, he felt the unfamiliar softness of his own body shifting beneath his clothes. His waist had lost its definition, expanding into something gentler, rounder. His chest, once hard planes of muscle, had developed a new fullness that disturbed him when he noticed it in the mirror, though he forced himself not to think about it too deeply. His arms, while still capable of the work, trembled slightly after an hour of sustained effort, the endurance sapped from his muscles in ways that felt like aging accelerated, though he was only thirty-four.

He told himself it was the job. The sedentary nature of finish carpentry—hours of precise measurement and careful joinery rather than the raw hauling and cutting of rough construction—had simply caught up with him. He told himself he had been too comfortable, too willing to accept Jane's afternoon interruptions, too quick to abandon his gym routine in favor of sitting with her on the veranda, drinking tea and discussing the finer points of Victorian architecture while his muscles atrophied from disuse. He told himself it was laziness, pure and simple, a man grown soft from easy living and a woman's flattering attention.
